text:
This section examines Chapter 0 — Cold
open: the same

pieces, a different result (2–3 minutes)
from first principles. Keep

two questions separate: does changing the
order change the measured

outcome, and does the proposed search
method beat a matched

alternative at the same
distinct-evaluation budget? Open on six

instruction cards. Run the same arithmetic
question through two different

orders. One ordering produces a poor
result; the other produces

a correct result. Do not initially reveal
prism. Then show:

> “What if the components are already
fixed, but their

order is the hidden variable?” Reveal the
paper title, author,

affiliation, and central question. Preview
three headline observations

without turning them into unsupported
causal claims: six LLM instruction

modules produced a 6.3%–96.9% accuracy
range across orderings; six sin-dee

preprocessing components produced
0.1%–23.2% recovery error; some landscapes

gave evolutionary search no advantage over
random sampling. End with

the film’s thesis: prism became a protocol
for deciding whether

and how an ordering problem should be
searched. The distinction

is part of the result. A large ordering
effect does

not automatically imply an
evolutionary-search advantage, and

convergence does not promise practical
efficiency.
